about.title: Lincoln Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Lincoln has grown quickly, and with that growth comes more households buying appliances, tools, vehicle parts, and consumer goods locally and online. When one of those products fails — because of a design flaw, a manufacturing error, or a missing warning — the person hurt is often left with medical bills and no clear idea who's responsible. California law helps here: under strict liability, you generally don't have to prove a manufacturer was careless, only that the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. That can include the maker, the distributor, or the retailer who sold it. If you were hurt by a product anywhere in Lincoln, from a home near Joiner Parkway to a business along Lincoln Boulevard, keeping the product itself and any packaging is one of the most useful things you can do early on. LawProactive connects you, free of charge, with an independent attorney who can look at what happened and explain your options.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: No. California's strict liability rule generally lets you focus on showing the product itself was defective — in design, manufacturing, or warnings — and that the defect caused your injury. You don't need to dig into whether the company acted negligently. An independent attorney can walk you through how this applies to your situation.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep it exactly as it was when the injury happened, including packaging, instructions, and any parts that broke. This is true whether the incident happened in a Lincoln home near Twelve Bridges Drive or anywhere else. Preserving the product helps an attorney and any experts evaluate the defect claim.
